instruction: I want to manually enter my information each time instead of using autofill. Can you turn off Chrome's autofill feature?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"autofill":{"profile_enabled":true}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to disable Chrome's autofill feature. The evaluator checks autofill.profile_enabled in Chrome Preferences. Initial state: true (autofill enabled). Expected state: false (disabled). Getter returns 'true' when disabled to match expected 'true'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks autofill.profile_enabled setting in Chrome Preferences
Postconfig properly restarts Chrome to ensure preferences are persisted and loaded
Getter extracts the correct state from the right file path (supports Windows, macOS, Linux)
Logic will work correctly at runtime - when autofill is disabled (profile_enabled=false), getter returns 'true' which matches expected 'true'
Complete coverage - single-step task fully verified
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Inverted return logic is semantically confusing: getter returns 'true' when autofill is disabled. Consider either: (1) Return actual state 'false' when disabled and set expected='false', or (2) Rename getter to 'get_autofill_disabled__980fd38b' to match inverted semantics
